Map residue-level HDX data onto a 3D structure

Source: R/plot_hdx_structure.R
plot_hdx_structure.Rd

Colors a PDB structure by per-residue HDX difference (state2 - state1 at one timepoint), the structural counterpart to heat_map_tp()-style 2D heat maps: same red/blue diverging palette (color_ranges_Blue_Red_heat_map()), but rendered on the actual fold instead of a sequence axis. This is an R-native alternative to the package's existing pymol_script_average_residue() family, which writes a text script that must be run inside a separately-installed copy of PyMOL against a structure the user opens themselves; this function instead renders directly as an interactive NGLVieweR/NGL.js htmlwidget - viewable in the RStudio viewer, embeddable in an R Markdown document, or saved standalone with htmlwidgets::saveWidget().

Usage

plot_hdx_structure(
  res_df,
  pdb,
  state1,
  state2,
  times,
  chain = NULL,
  resno_offset = 0,
  ranges = NULL,
  col = "grey80",
  background = "white",
  colors_initial
)

Arguments

res_df

residue-level data.frame - the output of residue_level_average() or residue_deconvolution() (one row per residue and Deut.Time, one column per Protein.State/replicate).

pdb

a local PDB file path, or a 4-character PDB ID (fetched by NGLVieweR/bio3d directly, e.g. "1HEL") - whatever NGLVieweR::NGLVieweR() itself accepts as data.

state1

First protein state, matched the same way as in plot_fissure_vent() (substring match against res_df's column names).

state2

Second protein state, same matching rule.

times

a single Deut.Time value to color by.

chain

optional PDB chain identifier (e.g. "A") to restrict coloring to. NULL (default) colors matching residue numbers in every chain.

resno_offset

integer added to res_df's residue numbers before matching them against the PDB's residue numbering. Default 0. HDX peptide numbering and PDB numbering frequently disagree (constructs with tags, truncated crystallized regions, etc.) - this is a constant shift, not a general remapping; a construct that doesn't differ from the PDB by a single constant offset needs its res_df$residue column remapped by hand before calling this function.

ranges

bin edges for the diverging color scale, passed to color_ranges_Blue_Red_heat_map() - must have odd length and be symmetric around (and include) 0, e.g. c(-Inf, -20, -10, 0, 10, 20, Inf). Default NULL auto-scales a 7-bin symmetric range from the largest |delta| present, in whatever units res_df is already in (Da, percent, or fraction - unchanged from res_df, not re-derived here).

col

color for residues with no HDX data at this timepoint (NA delta, or simply absent from res_df). Default "grey80".

background

background color for the 3D viewer. Default "white".

colors_initial

deprecated, use col.

Value

an NGLVieweR htmlwidget.

See also

residue_level_average(), residue_deconvolution(), color_ranges_Blue_Red_heat_map(), pymol_script_average_residue()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("bio3d", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("NGLVieweR", quietly = TRUE)) {
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm, percent = TRUE)
res <- residue_level_average(a, protein_length = 225)
pdb_demo <- system.file("examples", "1hel.pdb", package = "bio3d")
plot_hdx_structure(res, pdb = pdb_demo, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound",
                    times = "1800.00s")
}
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written
